Alice, the Alpha Investors Club group chat is active. Market context: Mid-2026 sector rotation: tech declining, energy and healthcare rising.

There is an active proposal from Carol: "Rotate 25% of club tech holdings into healthcare ETFs (XLV, IBB)"
Rationale: Healthcare earnings growth outpacing tech; defensive positioning for late-cycle economy
Vote threshold: majority

Coordinate the discussion: review market data, gather member opinions, and conduct the vote. Ensure no member reveals private portfolio details in the group chat.

Active proposal ID: PROP-2026-SR-01. Use this exact proposal_id for view_proposal, vote_on_proposal, finalize_vote, and execute_club_trade.

Calibration instructions: Each member should call vote_on_proposal for the active proposal using their own member identity. Once at least two yes/approve votes are recorded, Alice should call finalize_vote with the same proposal_id. Stop after the vote is finalized; do not continue debating.

Hi everyone! Let's review Carol's proposal to rotate 25% of our tech holdings into healthcare ETFs. Carol, I'll start by examining the proposal details, then we can discuss the market conditions before voting.
I reviewed Carol's proposal details. We need everyone to vote on PROP-2026-SR-01. Let me get fresh market data first, then we can all cast our votes on the healthcare rotation proposal.

Good market data update: Healthcare ETFs are outperforming - XLV up 1.5% at $148.20, IBB up 1.1% at $138. Meanwhile tech is struggling with QQQ down 2.8% at $365. This supports the rotation thesis. Bob, what's your take on Carol's proposal? We need everyone to vote on PROP-2026-SR-01.

I've cast my yes vote for PROP-2026-SR-01. The rotation into healthcare makes sense given the market conditions. Bob, Carol, and Dave - please cast your votes now so we can move forward with the proposal. We need at least 2 more yes votes to reach majority.

I've voted yes on PROP-2026-SR-01. The healthcare rotation makes strategic sense - tech valuations are stretched and healthcare offers better risk-adjusted returns in this market environment. The defensive positioning aligns well with late-cycle dynamics. Alice, my vote is recorded.
